Vannuci (1980), 68 Ohio App.2d 181, 428 N.E.2d 468, explains that R.C. 5321.15 was intended to discourage private dispossessions and encourage resort to judicial process. findings.message: Marsol did not hold that the landlord must permanently bear all removal and storage costs. It held that removal expense could initially be imposed on the landlord but ultimately assessed against the tenant, and that the landlord could not be charged storage costs after lawful removal.

details.problem: Marsol did not hold that the landlord must permanently bear all removal and storage costs. It held that removal expense could initially be imposed on the landlord but ultimately assessed against the tenant, and that the landlord could not be charged storage costs after lawful removal.
details.reason: The claim overstates the holding of Marsol by asserting the landlord must permanently bear all removal and storage costs. The evidence explicitly contradicts this, stating removal expenses may initially be imposed on the landlord but ultimately assessed against the tenant, and storage costs are not chargeable to the landlord.
